findings.title: Sub-second performance target has no timing or load test
findings.description: The design restates "detection adds under one second to a Phase 0 build on a local disk" (slice design line 167). Line 38 says there is no timing or load test, because the `tests/load/` tier "is a rule in `rules/python.md`". The breakdown is right that the rule is Python-named. But the rule's trigger is event-loop, concurrency and budget risk (`python.md:57`), and D2 itself says the walk must not block the MCP event loop. The caps tests bound the work but never measure time. Either add a load or timing task for a large tree at the caps, plus a CI gating task for it, or record a PM-approved waiver in the slice. The only `tests/load` reference in the worktree is that python rule.

findings.title: Commit points are checkbox items, not `**Commit**:` markers
findings.description: The ten commit points (lines 78, 105, 131, 148, 178, 202, 225, 251, 257, 269) are `- [ ]` checkboxes. The convention is plain `**Commit**:` lines, never checkboxes, and the order is implement, then task-checker, then commit. A box for a commit cannot be checked inside the commit it triggers, so either the commit ships an unchecked box or a change lands after it. Convert each to a plain `**Commit**: feat(core): ...` line under its group's last task. The cadence itself is correct.

findings.title: Detection's source walk imports the policy threshold from `adoption/`
findings.description: Task 3 has `detection/sourceVolume.ts` import `BROWNFIELD_MIN_SOURCE_LINES` from `adoption/adoptionOutcome.ts` as its stop threshold. The design says detection is "facts only, no policy" and thresholds live in `adoption/` (slice design line 106). Now `adoption/adoptionOutcome.ts` depends on detection's `SourceVolume` type and detection depends on adoption, a two-way dependency that Task 7 handles only with `import type`. Pass the threshold in instead: `measureSourceVolume(root, { stopAtLines })`, with the resolver supplying the constant. `contracts.ts` imports nothing, so importing `AdoptionError` from it is fine.

findings.title: Walkthrough step 1 hardcodes `main` and uses a worktree git may refuse
findings.description: The step builds `/tmp/before.md` from `main` through `git worktree add` of `main`. Two problems. First, the Git Rules say to read the target from `cf config get git.integration_branch` and never infer it, and that key exists in this repo. Second, `git worktree add <path> main` fails when `main` is checked out in another worktree, including the primary tree. Read the target first and use `git worktree add --detach <path> <target>`. The design's walkthrough (line 352) makes the same `main` assumption; the task inherits it.

findings.title: Missing-profile error is not tested through `context_build` or the `cf build` exit code
findings.description: Design line 333 requires `cf build` to exit non-zero and `context_build` to return the `AdoptionError` as an error. Automated tests stop at the integrator and pipeline (Task 10T, Task 12 #12). Task 11's `contextTools.test.ts` assertions cover only the `stateWrites` argument. The CLI exit is checked only manually in walkthrough step 4, and no task covers the MCP error result. Add to Task 11: a stub pipeline that rejects with `AdoptionError` makes the tool return an error result carrying the message, and a `build.test.ts` case for the non-zero exit.

findings.title: Renderer tests skip three of the five outcomes
findings.description: Technical Requirements (design line 336) require `renderAdoptionFacts` tests for "every outcome". Task 8T covers brownfield, adoption-in-progress and `NOT_EVALUATED` only. Add greenfield, already-planned and adoption-closed (both `complete` and `declined`). Task 8 also specifies that state `''` renders as unset, but 8T does not test it.

findings.title: The root for history and present-path facts is left implicit in the resolver
findings.description: D5 (design line 200) says every fact uses `checkoutPath`, and only the guide check uses `projectPath`. Step 6 names `recognizeCi(checkoutPath)` but not the root for `readHistory` or `presentPaths`. A worktree build could pass `projectPath` by mistake. No test in 9T uses `projectPath` different from `checkoutPath`. Name `checkoutPath` for every fact and add one 9T case that splits the two paths.

findings.title: Write-failure test omits the "state unchanged" assertion
findings.description: Technical Requirements name "D9's write failure (`AdoptionError`, state unchanged)" (design line 336). Task 9T asserts only the error and its remedies. After the failed write, read `adoption.state` back and expect `''`.

findings.title: Walkthrough step 2 names no public repository
findings.description: The step clones "a real public codebase over 2000 lines" without naming one, so the run is not repeatable. Name one repository with a commit SHA and record both in the walkthrough.

findings.title: Task 2 adds an `AdoptionError` trigger that D9 does not list
findings.description: D9 (design line 246) says `AdoptionError` covers three failures. Task 2 adds a fourth: a hand-edited `adoption.state` outside the enum. That fits the no-silent-fallback rule, so keep it, but add it to D9's list.

findings.title: Optional resolver and `projectPath` guard can silently produce the concept prompt
findings.description: Task 10 makes the resolver `= null` and calls it only "when the resolver and `project.projectPath` are set". An integrator built without a resolver, or a Phase 0 build without `projectPath`, quietly gets the concept prompt, which the core rules forbid as a silent fallback. The required `createContextPipeline` option covers production wiring. Consider failing explicitly when a Phase 0 build has no `projectPath`.

findings.title: The ENOENT-mid-walk skip has no test
findings.description: D2 (design line 171) makes ENOENT during the walk "not present". Task 3 implements it, but Task 3T tests only the non-ENOENT throw. Add one test that mocks `lstat` to return ENOENT for one entry and asserts the walk skips it.

findings.title: Task granularity is proportionate, with two small cuts
findings.description: One task file is the right size for this slice. Task 4 and Task 5 share commit 5C, and Task 7 and Task 8 share commit 8C, so each pair could merge into one task. Drop the legacy `resolvePhaseValue('phase 1: concept')` assertion at line 61, since no criterion needs it. Converting the commit checkboxes also removes ten items.

findings.title: Success criteria are covered end to end, except the gaps above
findings.description: Each functional bullet (design lines 322–333) maps to a task: the Phase 0 fixtures in Task 12 #1–#13, the selection table in Task 9T, CLI/MCP parity in Task 13, and the walkthrough in Task 15. Technical Requirements map to Tasks 3T, 4T, 5T, 6T, 7T, 8T, 9T, 11 and 15, with the gaps listed above. The integration requirements are structural (exports from `adoption/`, `renderSquadronFact`). Nothing from the Excluded list is built, and no merge or push appears as a task.

findings.title: Sequencing, test-with pattern and dependencies are sound
findings.description: Every implementation task is followed by its test task (1/1T through 10/10T). The dependency chain has no cycles: 1 → 2 → 3 → 7 → 8 → 9 → 10 → 11 → 12/13. Commit points fall at tested group boundaries, not after every task.
